CheckTitle: VM OS disks are encrypted with CMK
Description: Verify that OS disks of Virtual Machines are encrypted using Customer-Managed Keys (CMK).
Risk: Default encryption is managed by Microsoft. CMKs provide greater control over disk encryption keys.

Code.Other:
1. Stop/deallocate the Virtual Machine: az vm deallocate -g <resource-group> -n <vm-name>
2. Identify the OS disk name: az vm show -g <resource-group> -n <vm-name> --query 'storageProfile.osDisk.name' -o tsv
3. Update the disk with a Disk Encryption Set (DES): az disk update -g <resource-group> -n <os-disk-name> --encryption-type EncryptionAtRestWithCustomerKey --disk-encryption-set <disk-encryption-set-id>
4. Start the Virtual Machine: az vm start -g <resource-group> -n <vm-name>

Recommendation.Text: Enable Customer-Managed Keys for VM OS disk encryption.
